hints: At constant speed, acceleration is zero, so the forces parallel and perpendicular to the inclined plane are in equilibrium.
Resolve perpendicular to the plane to find the normal reaction: $R = mg\cos 6^\circ$.
Because the block moves up the plane, friction acts down the plane: $F = \mu R = 0.3(50\cos 6^\circ)$.
Resolve parallel to the slope: $T = mg\sin 6^\circ + F$, and evaluate $T$.
walkthrough:
Resolve perpendicular to the inclined plane to determine the normal reaction force $R$:
$$R = mg\cos 6^\circ = 5(10)\cos 6^\circ = 50\cos 6^\circ \approx 49.7261\text{ N}$$

Calculate the limiting frictional force opposing upward motion:
$$F = \mu R = 0.3 \times 49.7261 \approx 14.9178\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces parallel to the plane in equilibrium ($a = 0$):
$$T = mg\sin 6^\circ + F$$
$$T = 50\sin 6^\circ + 14.9178 = 5.2264 + 14.9178 = 20.1442\text{ N} \approx 20.1\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the equilibrium condition perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$\Sigma F_{\perp} = 0 \implies R - mg\cos 6^\circ = 0$$
Substitute $m = 5\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R = 5 \times 10 \times \cos 6^\circ = 50\cos 6^\circ$$
$$\cos 6^\circ \approx 0.994522 \implies R = 50 \times 0.994522 = 49.7261\text{ N}$$

State the kinetic friction formula for motion along the surface:
$$F = \mu R$$
Substitute $\mu = 0.3$ and $R = 49.7261\text{ N}$:
$$F = 0.3 \times 49.7261 = 14.9178\text{ N}$$

State the equilibrium condition along the line of greatest slope for constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$\Sigma F_{\parallel} = 0 \implies T - mg\sin 6^\circ - F = 0$$
$$T = mg\sin 6^\circ + F$$

Substitute the numerical values:
$$mg\sin 6^\circ = 50\sin 6^\circ$$
$$\sin 6^\circ \approx 0.104528 \implies 50\sin 6^\circ = 5.2264\text{ N}$$
$$T = 5.2264 + 14.9178 = 20.1442\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $T = 20.1\text{ N}$.
